readers.reasoning: Each pointer (t.l->c in one mid, t.r->c in another) has its own attachment counter; t is present when the members are copied in, so attach of t.r->c to the already-present leaf is a normal increment/attach. Deletes only decrement reference counters; the leaf being deleted twice is a no-op once absent. Sum is 5+2*(1+2+3+4)=25. The runtime error 'enclosing struct not mapped for attach' contradicts the data model.

Each pointer is attached after its parent is present: t, then t.l[0:1], t.l->c[0:1], t.l->c->a[0:4], then t.r[0:1] and t.r->c[0:1] (leaf already present, count incremented, attach). Device reads give 5+2*10=25. Deletes run children first, and the leaf's counter is decremented twice, so each delete finds it present or does nothing. The runtime error 'enclosing struct not mapped for attach' is a compiler defect. Slight uncertainty on shared-leaf attachment detail.

copyin(t) maps the struct, then each member target is mapped after its enclosing struct, so each pointer attach has its enclosing object present. t.r->c aliases t.l->c: the second copyin only increments the dynamic reference counter and attaches t.r->c. Each delete without finalize only decrements the counter, so the shared leaf stays until both deletes run. Sum is 5+2*(1+2+3+4)=25. libgomp's 'enclosing struct not mapped for attach' is a compiler bug.

t is shallow-copied, then t.l, t.l->c, t.l->c->a, t.r and t.r->c are copied in with attach actions. The shared leaf is entered twice (dynamic counter 2) and deleted twice without finalize, so counters return to zero; delete of an absent or zero-counter item takes no action. Each parent pointer is attached under its present enclosing struct. The attachment-counter model permits two pointers to one target. The libgomp error about an enclosing struct is an implementation limitation.
